caseno: Civil Revision No. 1461 of 2003 with Civil Revision No. 1462 of 2003.
lawyer:
Hasan Foez Siddique with Md Habibullah, Advocates—For the Petitioners. (in both the Rules). 
Md Lutfor Rahman Mondal with KM Zahid Sarwar, Advocates—For the Opposite Parties. (In both the Rules).
parties:
Tara Bibi alias Tahera Begum & ors ----- Defendants-Petitioners 
vs. 
Salma Rani & ors  ----- Plaintiffs-Opposite
full_judgment:
The Rule in Civil Revision No. 1461 of 2003 is directed against the judgment and decree dated 30-11-2002 passed by the learned Additional District Judge-in-charge, 5th Court, Dhaka, in Title Appeal No. 181 of 1999 (heard analogous with Title Appeal No. 182 of 1999) dismissing the appeal and affirming the judgment and decree dated 25.2.1999 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge and Commercial Court No. 1, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 23 of 1992 (heard analogous with Title Suit No. 22 of 1992) decreeing the suit.

2. The Rule in Civil Revision No. 1462 of 2003 is directed against the judgment and decree dated 30.11.2002 passed by the learned Additional District Judge-in-charge, 5th Court, Dhaka, in Title Appeal No. 182 of 1999 (heard analogous with Title Appeal No. 181 of 1999) dismissing the appeal and affirming the judgment and decree dated 25.2.1999 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge and Commercial Court No. 1, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 22 of 1992 (heard analogous with Title Suit No. 23 of 1992) dismissing the suit.

3. Short facts necessary for disposal of the Rule are, that the predecessor-in-interest of the Opposite Party Nos. 1-14 named Emdaduddin, as plaintiff instituted Title Suit No. 480 of 1978, subsequently renumbered as Title Suit No. 23 of 1992 in the 1" Court of learned Subordinate Judge, Dhaka impleading Md Soleman, the predecessor-in-interest of petitioner No. 1 of this Rule seeking for the following relief:

"10. The plaintiff, therefore, prays:

a) that a decree may be passed in favour of the plaintiff and against the defendant by declaring that the plaintiff is the sole sixteen annas owner of the entire suit property;

b) that a decree for recovery of khas possession of "B" Schedule land by removing all obstructions there from may be passed in favour of the plaintiff and against the defendant;

c) that a decree for confirmation of possession of the "A" Schedule land may be passed in favour of the plaintiff and against the defendant

d) that all costs of the suit may be awarded in favour of the plaintiff and against the defendant;"

Contending, inter alia, that the suit property belonged to Md Soleman, the defendant who sold the entire suit property in favour of the plaintiff by a registered Kabala deed dated 13-11-1973. After purchase Md Soleman was accorded permission to stay in the "B" Schedule land to the plaintiff as a licensee for few months. On December 1973 the plaintiff requested the defendant to vacate the "B" Schedule land and to deliver vacant possession in his favour but later refused. The cause of action arose on 19th December 1973 and, as such, the suit.

4. The defendant Md. Soleman Ali submitted a Written Statement on 3-5-1979 in Title Suit No. 480 of 1979, subsequently renumbered as Title Suit No. 23 of 1992 denying the material statements made in the plaint and contending, inter alia, that he is the sixteen annals owner of the property mentioned in the schedule 'A' and 'B' by purchase on the strength of a registered lease deed of perpetuity dated 4-6-1956 being No. 6096 and by a deed of purchase of Quit Rent, being No. 6097 dated 4-6-1956 on payment of proper consideration from real owners. Since the date of purchase the defendant has been owning and possessing the schedule "A" property by erecting new structures thereon and living with the members of his family and carrying on business in a portion of it on getting his name recorded in the record of rights and on payment of rent to the proper authority and his name was also duly mutated in the Dacca Municipality and he is also paying Municipal taxes, WASA and Electric bills. The plaintiff was known to the defendant for a pretty long time and he was a peon, serving at settlement office at Dhaka, used to come to the defendant in times of need for help and the defendant also helped the plaintiff in various ways and after liberation of Bangladesh the plaintiff having no accommodation for himself and his family at Dhaka, approached the defendant allowing him to live in "B" Schedule property as his licensee, which is a small portion of "A" schedule property and the defendant out of sympathy as licensee allowed the plaintiff to live in a portion of suit land. The defendant is a Non Bengali Urdu speaking person who came from India as a refugee in the year 1950, after partition of India. After liberation war of 1971 and creation of Bangladesh the defendant had to remain absent from his house for some time leaving the schedule property (house) and business establishment including machineries thereof in the care, custody and supervision of the plaintiff on whom the defendant reposed full confidence, belief and trust. After liberation and during the disturbed post -liberation period the defendant could not manage his business and other family affairs and he had to depend on the plaintiff for such management. At that relevant period the plaintiff disclosed that to manage the business establishment and to look after the schedule property he requires a Power of Attorney in his favour by the defendant and the plaintiff had been constantly pressing for the same. In that state of affairs, the defendant had no other alternative but to agree to the proposal of the plaintiff and accordingly, a Power of Attorney was being got drafted by the plaintiff and the defendant was taken to the office of the Sub-Registrar, Dhaka for such registration of the same but the Sub-Registrar refused to register the same, on the plea that no Non Bengali is permitted under the present law to authorise or register any document in favour of anybody without permission from Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka. Being failure to get Power of Attorney registered in favour of the plaintiff by the defendant the plaintiff on a subsequent date took the defendant before one Magistrate, 1st Class, Dhaka and he was made to swear an affidavit dated 3-2-1973 giving the plaintiff authority and power to manage the affairs of the defendant. Even after swearing the above affidavit the plaintiff made several attempts to get a Power of Attorney executed and registered in favour of the plaintiff by the defendant and the defendant was taken to the Sub-Registrar's Office but no Power of Attorney could be registered although several attempts were made by the plaintiff in this regard. Since after liberation the plaintiff has been living in the "B" Schedule property, which is a small portion of the north eastern portion of the "A" Schedule property as a licensee of the defendant. The plaintiff being a local man and the defendant being a non-local had to get his business managed and he was also required to do other family affairs of the defendant at the relevant period. Curiously enough, the defendant got a notice from the Settlement office in the 1st week of September 1977, in the absence of the plaintiff wherein the defendant found that the plaintiff had filed an objection petition for canceling the name of the defendant in respect of the "A" schedule property in the recent RS Operation and for getting his name recorded. On the date of hearing of the said Objection Petition No. 329 of 1977 the defendant was present and raised objection and produced the relevant papers and documents in support of his title in respect of the schedule property to the Settlement Officer who on perusal of the papers and documents in possession of the defendant was pleased to reject the prayer of the plaintiff and upheld the previous record stood in the name of the defendant for the schedule property. On getting the notice from settlement office the defendant got suspicious about the activities and trustworthiness of the plaintiff and later on, the defendant came to learn that the plaintiff dishonestly removed all his machineries including a printing press machine and other goods and articles of the defendant from the said holding causing a loss of huge amount of Taka to the defendant and misappropriated the said amount. Some time thereafter, the defendant got a show cause notice and adinterim injunction notice of the instant suit from the Court, and the defendant caused his appearance on 14-11-1978 in the said suit and prayed for time to file Written Statement and on reading the plaint, the defendant could firstly come to know that the plaintiff had got a fraudulent and forged sale deed registered in his name in respect of the "A" schedule property by false personification. Thereafter, the defendant obtained a certified copy of the said forged and fraudulent document on 3-4-1979 and definitely could come to learn that a forged, fraudulent, collusive and illegal document has been created in favour of the plaintiff on false personification of the defendant to grab the valuable property of the defendant beyond his knowledge and without making any payment of consideration money whatsoever. The defendant did not put signatures on the said alleged sale deed. His signatures on the alleged document have been forged by some other person. All signatures as contained in the said deed are not the signature of the defendant and the said deed is forged, fraudulent and collusive deed and the deed was created by false personification. The defendant did not execute any sale deed for a sum of Taka 7,000.00 or for any amount on or before 13-11-1973 or any other date in favour of the plaintiff in respect of the schedule property or any portion thereof. The defendant had no or has no necessity of selling his only residential scheduled property. The said false, forged, collusive and illegal document has been created by the plaintiff in collusion with the scribe and other witnesses of the said alleged deed by illegally influencing them and some other lower category staff of the Sub-Registrar's office without making payment of any consideration money whatsoever. At that time the valuation of the property was much more than Taka 7000. The defendant did not put any signatures on any papers for bringing out Income Tax and Capital Gain Tax Certificates. Any certificates produced for registration of the said forged sale deed must have been produced by the plaintiff forging the signatures of the defendant and the plaintiff must be prosecuted for the criminal acts done by him. No right, title and interest have been passed to the plaintiff on the strength of the said forged, fraudulent, illegal and void document and the plaintiff cannot seek any relief in the Court of law on the strength of the said forged, fraudulent, collusive, illegal and void document. The defendant is the lawful, rightful and absolute sixteen annas owner of the schedules properties. By creation of such a forged, fraudulent, illegal and void document the defendant's right, title and interest in the scheduled properties have not been affected in any way. The defendant informed the respectable persons in the locality about the illegal, fraudulent and collusive activities of the plaintiff and they made attempts to settle the matter amicably but failed. The defendant has filed the Title Suit No. 98 of 1979 in the 6th Court of Munsif, Dhaka against the plaintiff for cancellation of the said forged, fraudulent, collusive and illegal document and also for recovery of khas possession of the "B" schedule property as described in the schedule below after evicting the plaintiff therefrom.

5. The defendant Nos. 5-8 submitted a Written Statement on 14-2-1983 adopting the Written Statement submitted by the main defendant Md. Soleman and also claimed that they have purchased the suit property contending, inter alia, that Md Soleman was a Urdu-speaking man who came from India as a refugee in the year 1950, after partition of India and he was the owner and possessor of the entire suit property in his own right till his death. He could not read and write in Bengali. He always used to put his signature in English. He did not sign his name any where in any documents in Bengali. Md Soleman did not execute the alleged sale deed in favour of the plaintiff in respect of the suit holding. He had no reason or necessity to sell his only residential house—the suit holding. He had other sources of income to maintain his family. The plaintiff created the alleged sale deed fraudulently and in collusion with the scribe and other attesting witnesses without payment of consideration money whatsoever to grab the valuable property of said Md Soleman. The original owner Md Soleman did not put any signature on any papers for bringing out Income Tax and Capital Gain Tax Certificate. The plaintiff created the alleged sale deed in his favour by forging the signatures of said Md Soleman beyond his knowledge. His signatures on the alleged document have been forged by some other person. All the signatures as contained in the said deed are forged, fraudulent, void and collusive and are created by false personification. No right, title and interest have passed to the plaintiff on the strength of the said forged, fraudulent, illegal and void document, and the plaintiff cannot seek any relief in the Court of law on the strength of the said forged, fraudulent, collusive, illegal and void document. By creating of such a forged, fraudulent illegal and void document, the defendant's right, title and interest in the schedule properties have not been affected in any way. The original defendant late Md Soleman had filed the Title Suit No. 98 of 1979 in the 6th Court of Munsif, Dhaka and the said suit of transfer to the Court has been renumbered as being Title Suit No. 516 of 1981. For cancellation of the said forged, fraudulent, collusive and illegal document and also for recovery of khas possession of the "B" schedule property as described in the plaint of the said suit, after evicting the plaintiff there from. These defendants purchased the entire suit holding from the heirs and successors of late Md Soleman in the year 1982 and they have been owning and possessing the same since their date of purchase and, at present, they are the real owners and possessors of the said property

6. Md Soleman on receipt of the notice of Title Suit No. 480 of 1978 presented a Title Suit being No. 98 of 1979 on 6-4-1979 before the 6th Court of Munsif, Dhaka seeking for the following relief:

"23. The plaintiff, therefore, prays: (a) for passing of a decree for cancellation of the deed No. 27265 dated 13-11-1973 allegedly registered in Book No. 1, Volume No. 385 Pages 291 to 294 for the year 1973 of the office of Sadar Sub-Registrar, Dhaka, allegedly executed and registered by the plaintiff in favour of the defendant in respect of the schedule 'A ' property and for declaring the said deed as void and not legally binding;

(b)  ..................

(c) for passing a decree declaring that the plaintiffs are the rightful owners of the properties described in the schedule’s" and to deliver khas possession of the 'B' schedule property to the plaintiff after evicting the defendant there from with all his men and materials in execution of the decree;" imp leading Emdaduddin (the plaintiff of Title Suit No. 480 of 1978 and subsequently renumbered as Title Suit No. 23 of 1992 to be the sole defendant) incorporating the whole case as made out in the written statement of Title Suit No. 23 of 1992.

7. Emdaduddin, the defendant (the plaintiff of Title Suit No. 480 of 1978 subsequently renumbered as Title Suit No. 23 of 1992) submitted a Written Statement in Title Suit No. 98 of 1979 subsequently renumbered as Title Suit No. 22 of 1992 denying the material statements made in the plaint and incorporating the entire case as made out in the plaint of Title Suit No. 23 of 1992.

8. Thereafter, the Title Suit No. 480 of 1978 was transferred to the Court of learned Subordinate Judge and Commercial Court No.1, Dhaka and was renumbered as Title Suit No. 23 of 1992.

9. The Title Suit No. 98 of 1979 was also transferred to the learned Subordinate Judge and Commercial Court No. 1, Dhaka and was renumbered as Title Suit No. 22 of 1992.

10. Both the suits were taken up for analogous hearing and the learned Sub-ordinate Judge and Commercial Court No. 1, Dhaka framed the following issues:

(i) Is the suit maintainable as it stands framed?

(ii) Is the suit barred by limitation?

(iii) Whether the plaintiff and the defendant has got their title and possession in the 'A' schedule to the plaint and whether they are licensee under the plaintiff of the respective suits in respect of 'B' schedule land to the plaint?

(iv) Whether the plaintiff of Title Suit No. 23 of 1992 is entitled to get a decree for declaration of title and confirmation of possession in respect of 16 annals share in 'A' schedule land and entitled to get a recovery of khas possession in respect of 'B' schedule land to the plaint?

(v) Whether the kabala deed being No. 27265 dated 13-11-1973 in respect of 'A' schedule land to the plaint is forged and not binding upon the plaintiff of Title Suit No. 22 of 1992 and whether the said deed is liable to be declared cancelled and whether the plaintiff is entitled to get a decree for recovery of khas possession in respect of 'B' schedule land as against the defendant of the suit?

(vi) What more relief the plaintiff is entitled to get?

11. The Title Suit No. 23 of 1992 was taken up for trial as being the parent suit and evidence was led in the said suit.

12. During tendency of the suit the plaintiff Emdaduddion and the defendent Soleman had died and their heirs were substituted. In Title Suit No. 23 of 1992, the following persons were made defendant (1) the Chairman, Water and Sewerage Authority, Ramna Chamber (2) Circle Officer (Revenue), Kotwali Circle, (3) Executive Engineer, Dhaka Electric Supply, English Road, (4) Md Khairul Alam (5) Md Nur Alamgir (6) Md Mohiuddin Alamgir (7) Md Intaz Ali Miah.

13. The plaintiff of Title Suit No. 23 of 1992 examined 3 PWs. The kabala deed in question dated 13-11-1973 alleged to have been executed by Soleman in favour of the plaintiff was marked as Exhibit 1. Some rent-receipts showing payment of rent after filing of the suit was marked as Exhibit 2, 2(Ka) and one rent-receipt showing payment of rent on 15-4-1977 was marked as Exhibit 2(Kha). Electric bill paid by the plaintiff of Title Suit No. 23 of 1992 for the month of July 1980, July 1981 and May 1981 was marked as Exhibit 3, 3(ka) and 3(Kha) and one receipts showing payment of sewerage bill for the month of May, 1977 was marked as Exhibit 3. It is to be stated here that after the death of Soleman his heirs and legal representatives were imp leaded as plaintiff Nos. 1 (a)-1 (p) in the Title Suit No. 22 of 1992. In total 7 DWs were examined by the plaintiffs of Title Suit No. 22 of 1992 and their documents were admitted into evidence as being A(1)-A(7), B series, C, D, E, F, F(1), G, H, I, J, K(1), L, M series, N, 0 series, P, Q series, R series, S, T, U.

14. The learned Subordinate Judge and Commercial Court No. 1, Dhaka decreed the Title Suit No. 23 of 1992 and dismissed the Title Suit No. 22 of 1992 by the judgment and decree dated 25-2-1999. The plaintiff of Title Suit No. 22 of 1992 being aggrieved by the said judgment and decree preferred Title Appeal No. 182 of 1999 and defendant of Title Suit No. 23 of 1992 preferred Title Appeal No. 181 of 1999 as against the said judgment and decree.

15. Both the appeals were heard analogously by the learned Additional District Judge-in-charge, 5th Court, Dhaka who by a single judgment disposed off both the appeals and dismissed those appeals by the impugned judgment and decree dated 30-11-2002.

16. The defendants of Title Suit No. 23 of 1992 being aggrieved by the said judgment and decree have obtained Rule in Civil Revision No. 1461 of 2003 and obtained Rule in Civil Revision No. 1462 of 2003 as against the judgment and decree passed in Title Appeal No. 182 of 1999. Both the Rules having arisen out of the same judgment and having been disposed off analogously this Court took up both the Rules together for disposal analogously.

17. Mr Mohammad Habibullah, the learned Advocate for the petitioner, on appearing before this Court, submitted that the defendant of Title Suit No. 23 of 1992 having specifically pleaded that the Exhibit 1 was not executed by Soleman, that deed was created by false personification, and that no payment of consideration was made as against the said deed and Soleman did not execute the said deed it was the duty of the trial Court to decide specifically as to whether the said deed was executed by Soleman and any consideration was passed against the said deed. He submitted that the trial Court without giving any finding upon those vital facts decreed the suit in a slip shod manner. He further submitted that the defendant Nos. 5-8 have specifically pleaded in the Written Statement that Soleman was not conversant with the Bengali writing and could not know how to put his signature in Bengali but the deed in question was shown to have been executed in Bengali. He submitted the same to be a forged deed out and out. He further submitted that the defendant (the plaintiff of Title Suit No. 22 of 1992) by producing Exhibits D, K, M, Ml, O, O(1)-O(4) and also by adducing oral evidence has been able to prove the fact that Soleman used to put his signature in English, he did not put his signature ever in Bengali. He further submitted that the plaintiff of Title Suit No. 23 of 1992 had onus to prove due execution of Exhibit 1 by Soleman and also had onus to prove that consideration of Taka 7,000.00 was received by Solaiman as against the deed but the plaintiff has hopelessly failed to prove due execution of the said deed (Exhibit 1) and also failed to prove payment of consideration by adducing evidence either oral or documentary. He further submitted that the plaintiff of Title Suit No. 23 of 1992 also failed to prove that any possession was handed over in his favour on the strength of Exhibit 1. He submitted further that the learned Subordinate Judge and Commercial Court No. 1, Dhaka without coming to his own finding as to execution of Exhibit 1 by Soleman and as to payment of consideration as against Exhibit 1 and as to delivery of possession as against Exhibit 1, blindly and erroneously held the Exhibit 1 to be a valid deed, only upon considering the fact, that Soleman did not make any attempt for getting compared his admitted LTI with the LTI as contained in the back of page 1 of Exhibit 1. He further submitted that the plaintiff of Title Suit No. 23 of 1992 has sought for recovery of khas possession in the 'B' schedule land in the plaint against Soleman alleging him to be a licensee under him. But the Courts below neither gave any finding upon the said relief nor discussion and considered any evidence in support of the said positive case of the plaintiff. He further submitted that the plaintiff of Title Suit No. 22 of 1992 by adducing 7 DWs and by exhibiting huge number of documents have been able to prove that Soleman did not ever put his signature in Bengali during his lifetime. He submitted that they have been able to prove that the Exhibit 1 was a forged deed out and out and have been able to prove too that the plaintiff of Title Suit No. 23 of 1992 was given accommodation as a licensee in a part of the suit homestead, in 1972 but the trial Court and as well as the appellate Court without discussing a single evidence, adduced by the plaintiff of Title Suit No. 22 of 1992, illegally dismissed their suit and decreed the other suit and the appellate Court, being the last Court of fact neither discussed any evidence nor gave his own finding in affirming the judgment of the trial Court. He submitted that onus heavily lay upon the plaintiff of Title Suit No. 23 of 1992 to prove due execution of Exhibit 1. by Soleman, payment of consideration made by PW 1 and acceptance of said consideration by Soleman and handing over possession of the suit property by Soleman in favour of the PW 1 but the PW 1 having failed to do so by adducing evidence and the DW 17 by adducing oral and documentary evidence having been able to prove that the Exhibit 1 was a forged deed out and out, the judgment and decree impugned in the Rule are although concurrent is liable to be interfered by this Court in revision. He relied upon the case law upon onus of proving due execution of Exhibit 1 as reported in 1987 BLD (AD) 306.

18. Mr Md Lutfor Rahman Mondal, the learned Advocate for the opposite party on appearing before this Court, on the other hand, submitted that in view of section 101 of the Evidence Act, the burden of proof of the pleadings case cannot be shifted. He further submitted that the plaintiff of Title Suit No. 22 of 1992 came up before the Court with a specific pleadings but they failed to discharge their onus as per law. He further submitted that the Title Suit No. 23 of 1992 was filed during life time of Soleman and he died long after four years of filing of the suit but said Soleman did not make any attempt to compare the LTI as contained in the back of page No 1 of Exhibit 1 with his admitted LTI. He further submitted that no prayer was made by Soleman for making a comparison of the signature of LTI as contained in Exhibit 1 with his admitted signature and LTI to prove that the Exhibit 1 was not executed by Soleman. He further submitted that the Exhibit 1 was admitted into evidence and was marked as Exhibit 1 without having any objection from the defendant side. He further submitted that the Exhibit 1 being a registered instrument that carries a presumption of correctness and validity. In support of his contention he relied upon the case law reported in 1993 BLD (AD) 150 and the case of Abdullah and 3 others vs Abdul Hakim and others, reported in 20 DLR (SC) 205. He further submitted that the execution of Soleman has been proved beyond doubt by the plaintiff by adducing the evidence of PW 1 and PW 2 who corroborated each other. Mr Mondal submitted that the impugned judgment and decree being the judgment of affirmance there is nothing to interfere by this Court unless a strong case of no consideration of any evidence or no reading of any evidence or misreading of any evidence on record is made out. He relied upon the case law of Azifannessa vs Sakur Miah and others, reported in 30 DLR (AD) 41. He lastly submitted that the Exhibit 1 being a registered document and having been exhibited without any objection, the same shall be presumed to be correct and valid. In support of his contention he relied upon the decision reported in 1993 BLD (AD) 114.

<u>19. On perusal of the case law reported in 1993 BLD (AD) 114 it appears that our Appellate Division has held that the presumption of correctness of a Registered Document is a rebut table presumption and after giving due opportunity to the parties concerned the same can be rebutted. So, that decision goes against Mr Mondal. The presumption of correctness is not conclusive. On perusal of the Case law reported in 20 DLR (SC) 205 it appears that objection as to formal proof of document to be taken at earliest point of time. Here in the instant case the document Exhibit 1 itself is the questioned document. Its formal proof although was not objected initially but the very deed having classified to be a forged one, the defendant will not be debarred from questioning the validity of that deed. That decision does not apply in the instant suit.</u>

20. In reply Mr Mohammad Habibullah, the learned Advocate for the petitioner, submitted that the presumption of correctness of a registered documents does not carry any evidentiary value of correctness. He submitted that the presumption is always rebut table and he relied upon the decision reported in 7 BLR (AD) 306.

21. I have heard the learned Advocates of both the parties and considered their respective submissions.

22. On perusal of the judgment of the courts below it appears that neither the learned Joint District Judge and Commercial Court No. 1, Dhaka, being the trial Court, discussed and considered any evidence of the defendants of Title Suit No. 23 of 1992 nor the learned Additional District Judge being the last Court of facts made any discussion and consideration of any evidence of the plaintiffs of Title Suit No. 22 of 1992. So it appears that the judgments and decrees impugned in the Rule are based upon total no consideration of the evidence, both oral and documentary as adduced by the plaintiffs of Title Suit No. 22 of 1992 and the defendants of Title Suit No. 23 of 1992. It further appears that both the Courts below decreed the Title Suit No. 23 of 1992 upon assumption on saying অনুমতি হয় Mr Lutfor Rahman Mondal, the learned Advocate for the opposite parties in both the Rules, submitted that the judgment and decree impugned in the Rules being concurrent, there is no scope to interfere with those judgment and decree in revision. Mr Lutfor Rahman Mondal further submitted that this Court in exercise of its power under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure is not entitled to enter into the evidence. Mr Mondal in support of his argument cited the case law reported in 5 DLR (FC) 147 and the case law of Ajufannessa vs Safar Mia and others reported in 30 DLR (AD) 41.

23. On perusal of the case law reported in 5 DLR 147 it appears that the fact of that case is distinguishable from the fact of the instant case. That case law is not at all applicable in the instant case.

24. On perusal of the case law of Ajufannessa vs Safar Miah and others reported in 30 DLR (SC) 41 it appears that the said suit was a suit for declaration of title. The trial Court disbelieved the plaintiff's Dakhilas, which were marked as Exhibit 4 series and that finding was affirmed by the learned Additional District Judge in appeal. That concurrent finding were disturbed by the High Court Division in 2nd appeal and upon those disturbance of concurrent findings the Appellate Division held. "concurrent finding of file s as to the genuineness of the rent-receipts found by the two lower courts in 2nd appeal to the High Court, unless such finding is vitiated by error of law or procedure such finding is binding on the High Court." The above finding of the Appellate Division is by now the established principle of law. But in the instant case, the trial Court decreed the suit keeping totally out of consideration of the entire evidence of the plaintiffs of Title Suit No. 22 of 92 and the evidence of defendants of Title Suit No. 23 of 1992. So I am of the view that the above case law cited by Mr Mondal is not applicable in the instant case.

25. To meet the objection as raised by Mr Lutfor Rahman Mondal that concurrent finding of facts cannot be interfered by this Court, I felt necessity of extending my hands towards the judicial pronouncements of our Appellate Division giving authority to the High Court Division to interfere with the concurrent finding of facts based upon no consideration of material evidence on record, misreading of material evidence of record and also on total non-consideration of evidence on record.

<u>26. In the case of Sakhina Khatun and others vs Mansur Alam and others reported in 48 DLR (AD) 160 it has been settled that "there being a total non consideration of all the witnesses of the preempted, the learned Single Judge acted wrongly in refusing to exercise his revisional jurisdiction in a case where due to total non-consideration of the material evidence on record an erroneous decision has been arrived at occasioning a failure of justice. In that decision the concurrent findings of the trial Court, Appellate Court and of the High Court was set aside by our Appellate Division. The above authority, authorizes this Court to enter into the entire evidence of both the parties in view of the facts that admittedly the Courts below have given their findings upon no considering the entire evidence of the defendant of Title Suit No. 23 of 92 and the evidence of plaintiffs of Title Suit No. 22 of 1992.</u>

27. Before entering into the evidence for discussion and consideration let us decide as to whether the trial Court and as well as the lower appellate Court were justified in shifting the burden of proving the forged nature of Exhibit 1 upon the defendant of Title Suit No. 23 of 1992 and upon the plaintiff of Title Suit No. 22 of 1992 and was justified in decreeing the Title Suit No. 23 of 1992 for granting a decree for eviction of the defendant of Title Suit No. 23 of 1992 holding him to be a licensee under the plaintiff.

28. Mr Lutfor Rahman Mondal submitted that the burden of proof of pleadings case does not shift and submitted that the burden of proving that the Exhibit 1 is a forged deed was upon the defendant of Title Suit No. 23 of 1992 and upon the plaintiff of Title Suit No. 22 of 1992. Mr Mondal in support of his contention relied upon section 102 of the Evidence Act and upon the case-law of Kambhu Lakshmana vs Tangirala Venkateshwala reported in 2 DLR 82. On perusal of the said case law it appears that the fact of that case is quite distinguishable from the fact of the instant case and the cited case law has got no manner of application in the instant case.

29. The plaintiff in Title Suit No. 23 of 1992 filed the suit for declaration of title, confirmation of possession in schedule 'A' land and recovery of Khas possession in the 'B' Schedule land of the plaint against defendant Md Soleman alleging, inter alia, that Soleman sold the suit property to him by a Kabala deed dated 31-11-73 at a consideration of Taka 7000.00. Md Soleman by filing a written statement totally denied the said sale and denied his execution as contained in Exhibit 1. Md Soleman denied to have receipt of any consideration money as against the Exhibit 1. Md Solaiman categorically asserted the Exhibit 1 to be a forged deed and made out a case that the said Exhibit 1 was created by false personification. The defendant Nos. 5-8 being the subsequent purchasers from the heirs and legal representatives of defendant Soleman have stated categorically in their written statement that Soleman was a no Bengali and could not know how to write Bengali. Those defendants also brought a specific case that the plaintiff of Title Suit No. 23 of 1992 had created the Exhibit 1 by false personification with the help of scribe and witnesses of the deed. The plaintiffs of Title Suit No. 22 of 1992 also established a specific and distinct case that Soleman did not execute the Exhibit 1 and did not receive any single farthing towards consideration from the plaintiff of Title Suit No. 23 of 1992 as against the Exhibit 1. It is their case that the Exhibit 1 was created by Emdad, the plaintiff of Title Suit No. 23 of 1992 by false personification with help of the deed writer of Exhibit 1 and also with the help of witnesses as mentioned in the deed.

30. This is by now settled that whenever the execution of a deed is totally denied and a clear case of creation of a forged document is made out by false personification, in that case, the onus of proving due execution, payment of consideration and delivery of possession in the suit land entirely rests upon the alleged purchaser who claims title upon that deed. This view finds support from the case law reported in 47 DLR 248 and the case law reported in 44 DLR 79.

<u>31. In view of the above it is my considered view that the onus of proving of due execution of Exhibit 1 by Soleman and payment of consideration was rested upon the plaintiff of Title Suit No. 23 of 1992. The onus of proving of granting license to Soleman in 'B' schedule land was also rested upon the plaintiff of Title Suit No. 23 of 1992.</u>

32. Now let us consider as to whether the plaintiff of Title Suit No. 23 of 1992 by adducing PW 1, PW 3 could be able to prove due execution of Exhibit 1, payment of consideration as against that document and the fact of granting licence to Soleman by adducing legal evidence.

33. Mr Md Lutfor Rahman Mondal, the learned Advocate for the opposite party, took me to the judgments of the Courts below and Mr. Mohammad Habibullah, the learned Advocate for the petitioner, took me to the material evidence on record which is available.

34. On perusal of the decree passed by the trial Court, it appears that the learned Subordinate Judge and Commercial Court No. 1, Dhaka, without discussing and considering a single documentary evidence of the defendant and without discussing and considering the specific case of both the parties as to granting of licensee have passed the judgment and decree in a slipshod manner. From the judgment of the appellate Court it also appears that he being the last Court of fact has affirmed the judgment of the trial Court blindly in a very slipshod manner and without discussing and considering any evidence on record. On perusal of the Written Statement of the defendant Nos. 5-8, it appears that they taken a very positive case that Md Soleman did not know how to write in Bengali, he used to put his signature in English. The DWs adduced evidence in support of the said contention. The plaintiff of Title Suit No. 22 of 1992 has exhibited the passport of Md Soleman and that was marked as Exhibit B. It appears from Exhibit B that his name was written in English just at the bottom of his photograph as contained in the passport. It further appears that Soleman had sworn affidavit before the Magistrate, 1st Class on 6-11-1979 wherein he put his signature in English and that was marked as Exhibit 8. Another affidavit was sworn by Soleman on 3-2-1973 before the Magistrate, 1st Class, Dhaka and that was marked as Exhibit K(1), the signature as contained in the said affidavit was written in English. From the Exhibit M and M 1, it appears that Soleman was a merchant, and he entered into import trade contract under the Government of Pakistan by putting his signature in English in the year 1961. From the Exhibit 0 it appears that he made a correspondence to the Controller of Import and Export of the Government of East Pakistan and he put his signature in English and other documents the Exhibits 1, 2, 3, 4 were also signed in English by Soleman. The Exhibit K2 is another affidavit sworn by Soleman before the Magistrate, 1st Class on 20-5-1972 and that was also signed in English. On the other hand, there is not a single document produced by the plaintiff of Title Suit No. 23 of 1992 to prove that Soleman used to put his signature in Bengali. It is true, that the plaintiff of Title Suit No. 22 of 1992 ought to have taken positive step for comparing the LTI as contained in the back of the first page of Exhibit 1 with the admitted LTI of Md Soleman but from the record it appears that the suit came up for peremptory hearing after the death of Soleman.

35. In the instant case, the defendant of Title Suit No. 23 of 1992 having totally denied the execution of Exhibit 1 and having specifically asserted that the instrument was a forged one. The PW 1 had to prove due execution, payment of consideration. On perusal of the evidence of the PW 1 it appears that to prove the fact of execution of Md Soleman he has simply adduced in his examination-in-chief “নালিশী সম্পত্তি আমি ১৯৭৩ সনে ৭০০০ (সাত হাজার টাকা)দিয়া মোঃ সোলেমানের নিকট হইতে খরিদ করিয়াছি। দলিল নং ২৭২৬৫ তাং ৭-১১-৭৩ (প্রদঃ নং ১)এই সেই সাফ কবলা দলিল। নালিশী সম্পত্তি খরিদ করিবার পর আমাকে দখল বুঝাইয়া দেন।” Save and except this evidence there is no other evidence available on record to show that the PW 1 adduced any positive evidence to prove due execution made by Soleman. The PW 2 being another witness has adduced “বাদী মৃত সোলেমানের নিকট হইতে ক্রয় করিয়াছিলাম। ক্রয়/বিক্রয়ের সময় আমি উপস্থিত ছিলাম। বিক্রয়ের পর অর্ধেক অংশের দখল বুঝাইয়া দেয় এবং অবশিষ্ট অংশের দখল হস্তান্তরের জন্য সময় নেয়।” Save and except this evidence there is no other evidence to prove that Soleman put his signature upon Exhibit 1. The PW 3 also stated in his examination-in-chief that “বাদী ক্রয় করিয়া নালিশী সম্পত্তি প্রাপ্ত হইয়াছে।” This PW 2 and PW 3 are neither witness to the deed nor are scribes of the deed. Due execution can be proved by the following modes : (1) by calling as a witness a person who wrote the document; (2) by citing a witness who saw the writing down of the deed and saw to put signature by the executants upon the deed; (3) who is qualified to express an opinion as to the writing by virtue of section 47 of the Evidence Act; (4) by comparison of the handwriting as specified under section 73 of the Evidence Act; (5) by the admission of the person against whom the documents is tendered and (6) by expert evidence.

36. In the instant case the mode of proving as stated above in (3), (4), (5) and 6 are absent. From the Exhibit 1 it appears that the writer of the deed was Bachchu Miah and two other witnesses named Rafiqul Islam and A Kiron Shaheen put signatures as witness but those persons were not brought before the Court to prove due execution.

37. So far the writing of the Exhibit 1 and execution is concerned PW 1 was put a question:

“দলিলটা কোন জায়গায় বসিয়া লিখিয়াছে?” and he replied “দলিলটা সোলেমান মিয়া লিখাইয়াছে। তাহা কোথায় লিখাইয়াছে তাহা আমি বলিতে পারি না।” Thereafter, PW 1 was asked “দলিল লিখার সময় হইতে আজ পর্যন্ত কি আপনি খোঁজ নিয়াছেন যে, উহা কোথায় লিখা হইয়াছিল? at this he replied “কোর্টে লিখা হইয়াছে" Thereafter he was asked" খোঁজটা কবে নিলেন?" at this stage he replied "কথা হবার পর সপ্তাহ খানেক পরে শুনলাম তাহার বন্ধুর কাছে লিখতে দেওয়া হইয়াছে।" at one stage he was asked a question in the following form “সোলেমান কবে প্রথম কোন তারিখে জায়গা বিক্রির কথা বলিয়াছে?” at this he replied "১৯৭৩ সালের তারিখ মনে নািই জানুয়ারি বা ফেব্রুয়ারির মধ্যে হইতে পারে" Thereafter he admitted "৩/৪ মাস কথাবার্তার পর ফাইনাল হইল" Thereafter he admitted ফাইনাল হইবার ২ মাস পরে লেনদেন হয়। বিক্রির টাকা-পয়সার লেনদেন একদিনেই হইয়াছিল। "From this evidence it appears that the execution and payment of consideration was made in August 1973. Thereafter PW 1 was asked a question দলিল লিখার কয় দিন পরে টাকা পয়সা লেনদেন হইল? Thereafter he replied "রেজিষ্ট্রি যেদিন হয় সেদিন লেনদেন হয়।” From this evidence it is very much clear that actually Exhibit 1 was not executed in the usual course of normal business in view of the fact that the Exhibit 1 shows its date of execution on 6-11-73 and the date of registration on 13-11-73.

<u>38. On perusal of Exhibit 1, it further appears that the stamps used for the purpose of writing of the deed were purchased on 30-10-1973 and the fourth page was a demy paper. The date of execution mentioning "6-11-1973" was written in a different ink and by a different person as it appears from the said deed. The stamps used for the purpose of writing of affidavit in support of the transfer were purchased on 13-11-1973. From this it is very much incredible to believe that after purchase of stamps on 13-11-1973, how could a deed be executed on 6-11-1973. Moreover, the PW 2 did not adduce a single evidence that he saw execution by Md Soleman. From this evidence it is proved beyond doubt that the plaintiff of Title Suit No. 23 of 1992 hopelessly failed to prove due execution by Md Soleman. Moreover the DW 1 could not produce any document at the trial to prove Soleman used to put his signature in Bengali. Soleman entered his appearance in the suit through an Advocate and executed Vokalatnama in English. There is no evidence on record to believe that Exhibit 1 was executed by Soleman. So, it is my considered view that the plaintiff of Title Suit No. 23 of 1992 has hopelessly failed to prove due execution of Exhibit 1 by Soleman.</u>

<u>39. So far as payment of consideration is concerned the PW 1 was put a question in the following form দলিল লিখার কয় দিন পরে টাকা পয়সা লেনদেন হইল? he replied "রেজিষ্ট্রি যেদিন হয় সেদিন লেনদেন হয়।” Thereafter, he was asked the following question দলিল লিখার কয় দিন পরে টাকা পয়সা লেনদেন হইল? at this he replied "একমাস/দেড়মাস পরে লেনদেন হয়" It is the case of plaintiff of Title Suit No. 23 of 1992 that the deed was written some times before 6-11-1973 and thereafter the payment was made. So as per the PW 1, the payment was made in December 73 or January 1974. The PW 2 in his cross-examination has said "বাদী সোলায়মানকে সদর সাব রেজিষ্ট্রি অফিসের নীচের তলায় টাকা দিয়াছিল। সকাল ১০-৩০ মিনিটের সময় টাকা দিয়াছিল। ঐ দিন রেজিষ্ট্রি হয়।" This evidence is quite contradictory with PW 1. There is no other evidence available on record to show that any consideration was made. From the discussions made above it is crystal clear that no execution was made by Soleman and no payment of consideration was made as against the Exhibit 1. The Courts below having failed to discuss and consider this evidence have caused a serious miscarriage of justice by the impugned judgment and decree and the same is liable to be interfered by this Court in view of the case law of Sakhina Khatoon versus Mansur Alam, reported in 48 DLR (AD) 160.</u>

40. Let us decide the other issue that is, whether the plaintiff of Title Suit No. 23 of 1992 was accorded licence to be part of the suit land by Soleman or Soleman was accorded permission to reside in "B" schedule land to the plaint by PW 1. The evidences on record are sufficient to decide this question. The Courts below although did not decide this question specifically but the evidence having been found sufficient as adduced by the DW 17, I find that this issue should be decided by this Court to meet the ends of justice in view of the case of Kabir Ahmed versus Md Nurul Islam, reported in 4 MLR (AD) 1.

41. To decide the issue, let us discuss the evidence on record. Soleman's wife was examined as DW 2 who in her evidence adduced

“এমদাদ উদ্দিন পিয়নের চাকুরী করিতেন। আমার স্বামীর জানা শোনা লোক ছিলেন। মাঝে মাঝে আমাদের বাসায় আসিতেন সাহায্য নেওয়ার জন্য। তিনি পাকিস্তান সময় হইতেই আমাদের বাসায় আসা যাওয়া করিতেন। বাংলাদেশ হওয়ার পর উক্ত এমদাদ আমার স্বামীর নিকট হইতে কিছুদিন নালিশী সম্পত্তিতে থাকিবার জন্য অনুমতি চাহিয়াছিলেন এবং কিছুদিন পর চলিয়া যাইবে বলিয়া অঙ্গীকার করিয়াছিলেন। সেই মর্মে আমার স্বামী উক্ত এমদাদ উদ্দিনকে নালিশী সম্পত্তির সামান্য কিছু অংশে অর্থাৎ ৩ টি রুমে থাকিবার জন্য অনুমতি দেন। আমার স্বামীর সহিত তাহার কথা ছিল যে, আমার স্বামী যখন তাহাকে চলিয়া যাইতে বলিবেন তখন সে বাড়ী ছাড়িয়া চলিয়া যাইবে। এইরুপে কিছুদিন বাড়ীতে অবস্থান করা অবস্থায় উক্ত এমদাদ উদ্দিন আমার স্বামীর বিরুদ্ধে বর্তমান নং ২৩/১৯৯২ নং মোকদ্দমা ১৯৭৮ সালে করেছিলেন।”

From the cross-examination it appears that no damage was caused and those evidence remained unshaken.

42. DW 6 Abdul Hamid, in his examination-in-chief, adduced the following evidence "এমদাদ উদ্দিন পাকিস্তান আমলে সোলেমানের নিকট আসা যাওয়া করিত। এমদাদ উদ্দিন সেটেলমেন্ট অফিসের পিয়ন ছিল। এমদাদ উদ্দিন গরীব ছিল এবং সাহায্য এর জন্য সোলেমানের নিকট আসিত। এমদাদ উদ্দিন ১৯৭২ সনে মার্চ/এপ্রিল মাসে সোলায়মান সাহেবকে বলে যে, ছেলেমেয়ে অসুবিধায় আছি এবং তাহাকে কয়েক মাস থাকার অনুমতি দেওয়ার জন্য অনুরোধ করে এবং আরো বলে যে কয়েকমাস পরে চলিয়া যাইবে। উক্ত কথার উপর ভিত্তি করে সোলেমান তাহার বাড়ীতে এমদাদকে থাকতে দিয়াছে। বাড়ীটার উত্তর দিকে ২টা রুমে এমদাদ উদ্দিনকে থাকতে দেয়। প্রথম একটা রুম নিয়া পরবর্তীতে অসুবিধার জন্য আরো একটা রুম নেয়। থাকতে দেওয়ার ঘটনা ১৯৭২ সনের প্রথম দিকের ঘটনা। নালিশী বাড়ীর বাকী অংশতে সোলেমান সাহেব তাহার ফ্যামিলি নিয়া ছিল।”

<u>43. On the other hand, the plaintiff of Title Suit No. 23 of 1992 could not adduce any positive evidence to prove that Soleman was granted licence to stay in the "B" schedule land to the plaint. Upon consideration of the above evidence it is very much clear that in fact, no transfer was made by Soleman in favour of the PW 1 and the PW 1 was granted permission by Soleman to stay in a part out of the suit homestead. Both the Courts below did not discuss and consider the, above evidence. From the facts and circumstances and discussions made, I have no hesitation but to hold that the Exhibit 1 was not executed by Soleman, no payment in consideration was made against the said deed and no delivery of possession was made in favour of PW 1 on the strength of that Exhibit. The Exhibit 1 is nothing but a forged deed. The judgment and decree impugned in the Rule are not sustainable in law and are liable to be set aside. There is merit in the Rules.</u>

44. In the result, both the Rules are made absolute, however, without any order as to costs. The judgment and decree dated 30-11-2002 passed by the learned Additional District Judge-in-charge, 5th Court, Dhaka, in Title Appeal No. 181 of 1999 (heard analogous with Title Appeal No. 182 of 1999) dismissing the appeal and affirming the judgment and decree dated 25-2-1999 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge and Commercial Court No. 1, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 23 of 1992 (heard analogous with Title Suit No. 22 of 1992) decreeing the suit is hereby set aside. The judgment and decree dated 30-11-2002 passed by the learned Additional District Judge-in-charge, 5th Court, Dhaka, in Title Appeal No. 182 of 1999 (heard analogous with Title Appeal No. 181 of 1999) dismissing the appeal and affirming the judgment and decree dated 25-2-1999 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge and Commercial Court No. 1, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 22 of 1992 (heard analogous with Title Suit No. 23 of 1992) dismissing the suit is also hereby set aside. Title Suit No. 22 of 1992 is hereby decreed with cost and Title Suit No. 23 of 1993 is dismissed with cost. The kabala deed alleged to have been executed by Md. Soleman on 6-11-1973 and registered on 13-11-1973 in favour of PW 1, Emdaduddin is hereby declared void and the same is cancelled. The title of plaintiff of Title Suit No. 22 of 1992 is hereby declared and the possession of the opposite party plaintiffs of Title Suit No. 23 of 1992 in part of the suit land are nothing but permissive possession granted by Soleman. The plaintiff of Title Suit No. 22 of 1992 is entitled to get recovery of khas possession after evicting the plaintiff of Title Suit No. 23 of 1992, on execution of the decree. All further proceedings of Title Execution Case No. 1 of 1999 now pending in the Court of Subordinate Judge and Commercial Court No. 1, Dhaka appear to be not maintainable as being infructuous one. The defendant Nos. 5-8 being a purchaser during tendency of the suit, their title will be governed according to section 52 of the Transfer of Property Act.

Send down lower Court's record at once.

End.
